title: Straighten a leaning tabletop Christmas tree in its three-eye-bolt stand: ease one bolt out as the other screws in
instruction: Straighten the little Christmas tree in its stand so that it stands upright and firm.
context: A real Christmas tree goes into an eye-bolt stand in millions of homes each December (about 21.6 million real trees were bought in the US in 2023), and getting it to stand straight is the part people dread: the Real Christmas Tree Board calls the classic eye-bolt stand a two-person job. Here the tree is already gripped by all three bolts but leans 2.5 degrees. The trunk is caged, so it cannot be pushed upright, and screwing in the bolt on the lean side alone just jams against the other two: the bolt opposite must be eased out while the lean-side bolt goes in, by matched amounts (about 3.5 turns of each fine thread, regripping each eye every half turn), until the tree is plumb, then snugged so every cap grips and the tree stays firm when pushed.
setup: Positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y to the left) in cm; heights are above the table. Tree stand (Jack-Post Oasis 313-ST: green polypropylene, 33 cm (13 in) across the base, 17.8 cm (7 in) tall; fixed to the table, reservoir empty) centred at (34, 0): a bowl tapering to 24 cm across at its deck 10 cm up, and on it a collar 15.6 cm across with a 12.7 cm (5 in) opening, through which three zinc-plated steel 5/16 in-18 eye bolts point at the centre, 15 cm up: A at 120 degrees from +x (front left), B at 240 degrees (front right), C at 0 degrees (back). Each bolt: eye 26 mm across of 6 mm wire, 80 mm from the eye to its steel end cap (15 mm across, 9 mm long); 1.411 mm a turn, clockwise from outside screws it in. Centre spike tip 2 cm up. Tree: a reusable 3 ft tabletop tree (a 1-3/4 in (44.5 mm) hardwood dowel trunk, bare for 30 cm above the butt, carrying a 2 ft artificial pine top; brought to 1.5 kg; 91 cm tall from the butt, foliage 43 cm across at the bottom; a fresh-cut tree of the same size may be used instead); butt on the spike. Start: all three end caps on the bark, none tightened and the trunk leaning 2.5 degrees towards +y (top about 4 cm off), the caps' faces 27.6 mm (A), 17.8 mm (B) and 22.7 mm (C) from the stand's axis. Distractors (NVIDIA SimReady, loose): unlit pillar candle (decor_candle_a01, 7.4 cm across, 7.5 cm tall, 0.35 kg) at (50, 33); mug (dishware_mug_a01, 11.4 x 9 x 8 cm, 0.30 kg) at (48, -36), turned 138 degrees; notebook (misc_notebook_a01, 22.9 x 17 x 1 cm, 0.25 kg) at (66, -24), turned 100 degrees. Both grippers start open at their ready poses.
scoring: Read from the trunk's tilt (real trial: a digital angle gauge on the bare trunk), whether each end cap bears on the bark (real trial: a 0.05 mm feeler blade will not enter between cap and bark; simulator: the bark pushes the cap back along its thread with at least 3 N), a firmness probe, and the grippers' clearance (video). 1.0: the trunk within 1.0 degree of vertical, all three end caps bearing on the bark, every fingertip point of both grippers (each finger's tip and 3 cm up it) at least 3 cm from the trunk below the branches and from all three eyes, and the tree still (turning under 0.02 rad/s), all held for 2 s; then, with both grippers still 3 cm clear, the firmness probe passes: a 5 N horizontal push on the bare trunk 25 cm above the butt, towards bolt A, then B, then C (each ramped on over 0.25 s, held 1 s, then released for 0.75 s; real trial: a push gauge at a mark on the trunk) moves the treetop at most 3 mm under the load and leaves it within 1 mm of where it stood once released, with the trunk within 1.0 degree and all three caps bearing after each release (real trial: a ruler clamped level beside the treetop, read from a phone video). A failed or interrupted probe starts the 2 s hold over. 0.5: at the end, the trunk within 1.0 degree of vertical with both grippers 3 cm clear, short of full credit (for example a cap not bearing, or the probe moving the treetop more than 3 mm). 0.25: at the end, all three caps bearing and both grippers clear, with the trunk within 2.0 degrees of vertical but more than 1.0. 0: anything else, including the starting 2.5 degree lean and a gripper still on the tree or a bolt. Letting the tree flop scores 0 for the whole trial: the trunk at any time more than 6 degrees from vertical.
reset_notes: Set the tree plumb with all three caps lightly on the bark (angle gauge 0.0 +-0.1 degrees on two faces), then turn A out and B in by equal half-turns, C untouched, until the gauge on the trunk's left face reads 2.5 +-0.2 degrees with all three caps touching but not tightened: about 3.5 turns each, about 2 minutes. Put the distractors back on their marks. Nothing is consumed: the dowel-trunk tree is reused every trial; re-mark the push point at 25 cm if it wears.
fidelity: Full size: 3 ft tree, stand at its listed 13 x 7 in. Trunk pivots on the spike (two hinges), can't lift out; foliage seen only. Bolt threads are code: 1.411 mm/turn, no back-drive, a snug bolt stops (90 N); caps push 300 N at most. Rigid trunk and caps, so the probe tests contact, not bark give; real stand flex is untested. Probe force applied by the scorer. Stand fixed, reservoir empty. Tree, stand, bolts custom meshes; distractors SimReady.
